references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the raising of Jairus' daughter, where Jesus enters the house and takes the girl by the hand.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus allows only Peter, James, and John to follow him into Jairus' house, sending the others away.
Another occasion when Jesus took only Peter, John, and James with him—at the transfiguration on the mountain—showing that these three formed an inner circle among the disciples.
Mark's account of the transfiguration where Jesus again takes only Peter, James, and John with him, confirming their special role among the twelve.
In Gethsemane, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John further into the garden, once more showing the inner circle of disciples who witnessed special events.
The immediate context where a message from the synagogue ruler's house arrives saying that his daughter has died, and Jesus encourages Jairus to have faith.
The continuation of the account where Jesus raises the dead girl, showing what happened after he entered the house with only the chosen witnesses.
